newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle trade moderate at $72 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle trade moderate at $72 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Thursday traded at $72.00 per cwt, steady with last week's top price, in moderate volume, feedlot sources said.
About 10,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, and an estimated 20,000 traded in Kansas, according to private sources and USDA.
There was talk that several packers lowered bids to $71.00 from $72.00 as the day progressed, which slowed trading as owners resisted the lower bids.
Many cattle feeders reportedly opted to wait until next week in hopes of getting $73.00, sources said.
Packer resistance to higher asking levels were tied to a slump in wholesale beef prices.
However, some meat industry sources said that the lower prices were encouraging active beef sales and that packers would need to buy cattle next week to replace supplies.
Boxed beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.03 to $0.87 per cwt, with 219 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
